intro: Professionals and everyday users convert bars (bar) to atmospheres (atm) when working across metric and other standards in automotive tire inflation placards, hydraulic cylinder design, scuba diving tanks, and barometric weather tracking. One bar equals 0.986923 atmospheres, while 1 standard atmosphere equals 1.01325 bars. Whether you are verifying pressure specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Gauge Pressure (psig) vs. Absolute Pressure (psia)
items: This converter scales pressure magnitude directly between bar and atm. In automotive tires, HVAC, and compressed air systems, gauges display Gauge Pressure (referenced to ambient atmospheric pressure, ~14.696 psi or 101.325 kPa at sea level).
For thermodynamic gas laws (PV = nRT) or vacuum chamber calculations, convert gauge pressure to absolute pressure by adding local barometric pressure before scaling.

faqs.question: How many atmospheres (atm) are in 1 bar (bar)?
faqs.answer: There are 0.98692327 atmospheres (atm) in 1 bar (bar), which rounds to 0.9869 atm for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 standard atmosphere equals 1.01325 bars.

faqs.question: How do I convert bars to atmospheres (bar to atm)?
faqs.answer: To convert bars to atmospheres, use the formula: atm = bar × 0.98692327. For example, converting 2.2 bar gives 2.1712 atm.

faqs.question: What is 2.2 bars in atmospheres?
faqs.answer: 2.2 bars (bar) equals exactly 2.1712 atmospheres (atm) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
